content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate puffs are dry corn flakes coated with a sweet chocolate glaze. They have a crunchy texture and a pronounced chocolate flavor, making them a popular breakfast cereal and snack for both children and adults.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial chocolate puff cereal appeared in the 1970s.
The flakes are toasted under high pressure to achieve their crispness.
The chocolate coating is typically made from cocoa butter, sugar, and milk powder.
In many markets the product is fortified with vitamins and minerals.
Packaging often uses bright colors to attract children’s attention.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide a quick source of energy, convenient for an active start to the day.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Fortified versions often include iron, which is essential for blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Added calcium helps strengthen bones and teeth.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: A modest amount of fiber aids digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Added sugars can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The formula may contain milk, soy, or nuts, which are important to note for people with food allergies.

items.title: Glycemic index
items.content: The cereal has a high glycemic index, which can cause rapid spikes in blood glucose.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Some varieties contain artificial flavors and preservatives that may cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chocolate puffs are typically served with milk or yogurt. They can be added to smoothies, used as a topping for desserts, or eaten dry as a snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cereal in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the bag tightly closed to prevent moisture absorption.
